summary: While fixer session was completing an inherited interrupted rebase, a concurrent actor pushed from the same clone (reflog: 'update by push' 07:01:42 +0700, not executed by this session) and then deleted 246 tracked files from the working tree (~07:02:07), including src/, tests/, public/. A second clone at C:/Users/think/Project_v2/Deers-Rock concurrently ran npm test/vitest.
root_cause: Two agent sessions operated on the same git clone simultaneously without coordination. This session inherited a crashed session's mid-rebase state and completed it without first checking for concurrent actors (recent .git/index mtime, live node/git processes, other clones).
what_i_did_wrong: Did not check for concurrent actors before mutating shared repo state (rebase --continue). Detected the concurrency only after the working tree was shredded. No destructive action was taken by this session; recovery was evidence-preserving.
impact: Working tree of 246 tracked files deleted on disk; unknown-actor push of 5a3a048 to origin/main. No git objects lost; index intact; recovery via git restore . was complete (0 dirty entries, fsck clean, only dangling post-rebase objects).
recovery: Froze all mutations; polled status 30s for quiescence
git restore . restored all 246 files; verified via status/fsck
Rebased own 2 commits onto the actor's 4 newer commits (no overlap), pushed 93d25df..65fab97
lesson: Before any git mutation on a shared clone: (1) check .git/index and reflog mtimes vs wall clock, (2) list running node/git processes and sibling clones, (3) if a rebase/merge is inherited, confirm the prior session is actually dead.
